speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent; can you tell me exactly when your gait and limb ataxia first began? Also, have you noticed any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your arms or legs?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any slurred speech or difficulty swallowing, and have you noticed any changes in your vision, such as double vision or drooping eyelids? Has anyone in your family experienced similar symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of your uncontrolled Crohn's disease and recent start of natalizumab raises concern for a specific complication; have you experienced any fever, severe headaches, or memory changes in the last few weeks? Given your symptoms of ataxia and the medication history, I need to order an MRI of the brain immediately. REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain shows lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). T1/T2 images demonstrate multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement. Neurological examination confirms ataxic gait, evidence of ataxia on coordination tests, and right upper limb weakness (4/5 strength). Vital signs are within normal limits.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI confirms Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML), a serious complication of your natalizumab treatment. I will stop your current therapy immediately and coordinate with infectious disease and neurology for supportive care. DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML)
